cohort: The study analyzed 201 cases of critical obstetric-gynaecological conditions and maternal mortality in pregnant, laboring, and postpartum women from 22 regional institutions in the Turkestan region, Kazakhstan.
finding: 0.3% of maternal near misses were registered, with obstetric causes accounting for 58.2% and extragenital for 41.8%, and these near misses were 1.2 times more frequent in the postpartum period compared to the antenatal period.
